question: The ‘Via Pomerania’ is a planned expressway that will connect Ustka, Słupsk, Bytów, Chojnice and Bydgoszcz, creating an important new transport route in northern Poland. It is crucial for improving transport accessibility in the region, increasing road safety and reducing travel times, as well as for economic development and better connecting ports with the country’s main transport corridors. 1.

Has the Polish Government asked the Commission to extend the transport corridors as part of the planned review of the TEN-T network, and has it informed the Commission of the inclusion of the ‘Via Pomerania’ expressway in regional transport plans?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2025) The co-legislators adopted the current trans-European transport network (TEN-T) Regulation on 13 June 20241. The Commission does not plan to revise the TEN-T Regulation soon and has no correspondence with the Member States concerning a possible revision.

The Commission prepared the last revision over several years and was in close contact with Member States and stakeholders during this process. At the time, Poland advocated for an extension of the European Transport Corridors, in particular along the Eastern border. Poland has not informed the Commission about the inclusion of Via Pomerania expressway in regional transport plans.
